chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
The mukari and the jammal, when they are strong in their journeying, should shorten (the prayer).

key_terms.الْجَمَّالُ: The one who rides a camel by leading it (holding the reins)
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: The one who rides a camel by urging it (e.g., with a stick or voice)
key_terms.جَدَّ بِهِمَا السَّيْرُ: When they are strong/capable in their journeying (indicating the condition for shortening prayer)
key_terms.فَلْيَقْصُرَا: They should shorten (referring to the four-rak'ah prayer)

ai.seo_question: Who are the mukari and jammal and when must they shorten their prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific condition for shortening prayers during travel, linking the obligation to the physical exertion of riding a camel. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the hardship of travel, manifested here through the intensity of riding, triggers the concession of *qasr*, distinguishing between mere travel and travel involving significant physical strain.
